section.title: EDI, Who Has the Whole File
section.form_description: The narrator on their feet in a crowded room, speaking about someone who has died. Sections are the things there are to say about the dead — a habit, a fight, a debt, the once they were wrong, the once they were right when it counted. The tone swings: a story that gets a laugh, a line that lands angry, a stretch that can barely be got through. What holds it together is that none of it is polite — every word is meant.
section.form_note: The brief names the form outright: a memorial, six speakers on their feet, the eulogy's swing between a laugh, an angry line, and a stretch that can barely be got through. Jack is a deliberate exception to strict alternation and to normal voice balance - she opens and closes by the brief's fixed order, so she holds two of the seven turns while Tali, Grunt, Liara, Joker and Wrex each hold one. Her two turns are sized as ordinary single turns rather than doubled, but together they total roughly twice any other voice's word count, which is the "two turns' worth" the brief asks for. Section targets were raised after the voice checkpoint, at the user's instruction to let the speeches run to their natural length rather than be trimmed to a grid; the middle five now sit at 900-1200 (Joker's raised again after assembly, to carry the two illnesses beat in full) and the episode target at 6950. Each middle turn answers the one directly before it; Jack's closing turn answers the whole room, not just Wrex. Grunt's bible is new and unused before this run - he is built distinct from Wrex throughout: Wrex remembers the Rebellions and the genophage firsthand, Grunt states krogan history as Okeer's tank taught it and then flattens it to "put in me, not lived," and his own lived material is small and recent (the Rite, the Citadel, the mess hall, the war) and used in full. The "gets a detail wrong and is corrected" requirement is carried by two beats, not one: Grunt states the assumed version (died on his feet with a gun) and Joker mis-hears whose voice was on the channel, and Wrex corrects both flatly before giving the room the true version - shot on the way to the landing zone, then killed driving a vehicle into a banshee to clear passage for Hammer. Wrex reads that off the wreckage he found days later, not off memory; nobody in the room watched Thomas die, and each of them holds only a piece. No section narrates the Crucible's mechanism or Shepard as confirmed dead; Thomas's Synthesis sympathies, where they surface, are framed as a political stance he held in life, never as knowledge of the ending.

promises: answers Jack, who just said she was taking the poems away to read alone: EDI has them, recovered from his terminal, and has been holding them since

she speaks last because she is the only one who did not have to decide what to remember - she retells his life as the continuous record none of the others had: Akuze at twenty-one and walking out of the survey camp to find the only other survivor, the years teaching children robotics in Rouen, his mother, the burnout and the year with no work, Shepard remembering the tech from Akuze and calling him back in 2183, the SR-1, the two years after it burned, the SR-2 he hated serving on and stayed on anyway, Earth

Shepard and Thomas: met in the wreckage on Akuze as the only two left, and he followed Shepard everywhere afterwards - one of the very few Shepard confided in, and a real friend to him, not a subordinate. EDI can state the length and constancy of that as a fact none of the others can measure, and it lands hard in a room still waiting on Shepard
she names the limit of a record plainly: she has every fact about him and the least of him, and she says which of the others holds the part she does not

his coping mechanisms, which she is the only one who could see as a pattern rather than as personality: the humour that arrived a half-second after anything real, the analysis he could give of his own condition so precise it functioned as a way of staying above it, the cooking and fixing and feeding that regulated him as much as it fed anyone, the leaving first, and the version of himself he built for whoever was in front of him. She names them without diagnosing him and without calling any of them a flaw

and what those mechanisms did to his life and to the crew: the ship ate, the ship argued, the ship danced, and all of that was real and was also load-bearing for him. The crew received the adapted version and loved it, and he could not fully receive being loved because of which version had been loved - EDI can state that as a closed loop she watched run for years and could not intervene in. She says what the record shows anyway
what he brought to the ship, stated as observed effect rather than praise - the cooking nights, the readings, the arguments, the people who ate who otherwise would not have
what he brought to Jack, which EDI watched from outside and can describe in changes she measured: the heater, the messages, who Jack was before and after

what he brought to EDI: he argued she was a person while it was still an argument, addressed her as one before she was sure of it herself, and asked her questions instead of about her - she takes up the thing Joker said earlier about the roommate who came with the apartment
she reports one change in herself since the war that she cannot account for and declines to speculate about, and leaves the question open rather than closing it
the ethical problem she has been sitting with: she read the manuscript when she recovered it, which she is not certain she was entitled to do, and she says so before she sends it
she forwards the manuscript to Jack in the room, now

required_facts.fact: In 2177, an Alliance Marine unit is sent to investigate the settlement at Akuze, a human colony on the outskirts of Systems Alliance space, after all contact is lost with the pioneer team. The unit arrives to find the settlement intact but completely abandoned—no survivors are found. When the unit establishes camp for the night, they are attacked by subterranean thresher maws, creatures the Alliance has never encountered before. The unit is nearly completely slaughtered in the attack, with fifty marines killed and only one known survivor reaching the landing zone alive. If Commander Shepard is that sole survivor, Shepard is permanently marked by the trauma. Years later, Corporal Toombs is discovered to have also survived the attack. Toombs reveals a shocking truth: the massacre was not an accident. According to Toombs' testimony, the renegade black ops group Cerberus deliberately set the thresher maws on the marines as part of an experiment to study the creatures and observe how the unit responded to an unknown threat. Toombs was captured by Cerberus after the attack and subjected to horrific ordeals including being injected with thresher maw acid as part of their research. The revelation that Cerberus orchestrated the massacre haunts Shepard throughout the trilogy, becoming a symbol of Cerberus's willingness to sacrifice human lives for their research agenda.
Fifty Alliance marines are killed in the attack
Corporal Toombs survives but is captured by Cerberus for experimentation
Only one to two marines reach safety
A monument is erected at Akuze memorializing the fallen marines
Cerberus's involvement in the massacre is confirmed in recorded evidence

scenes.title: EDI Walks Out of the AI Core
scenes.when: 2186, aboard the Normandy just after Priority: Palaven

beats.text: Back from Menae, Joker reported a fire in the AI Core. Shepard went down to investigate and found EDI had transferred herself into the repaired body of Dr. Eva Coré — the Cerberus mech infiltration unit recovered from Mars.
EDI became a mobile squadmate from that point on, stationed in the cockpit beside Joker.

scenes.title: Goodbyes at the Forward Operating Base
scenes.when: 2186, Priority: Earth, before the armoured assault on the conduit
scenes.where: the Hammer Forward Operating Base in ruined London

beats.text: The evac shuttle off the first landing zone reunited Shepard with Admiral Anderson, who introduced Major Coats, the officer who had covered the extraction. Anderson said it had taken the Reapers to bring the galaxy together; a squadmate answered that Shepard was the true unifying force.

At the FOB, Coats told Shepard how inspiring the Commander would be to the troops, then left to rejoin his unit. Shepard walked the base holding final conversations with the surviving squad — as few as three or as many as seven, depending on who had lived through the trilogy and whether Javik had been recruited.

On a ramp Shepard found Primarch Victus and, if he lived, Garrus; past a husk turret gun, Liara, whose mood turned on how many husks had got through; then Javik and the krogan leader giving a rallying speech to the troops, with Kirrahe or another STG officer alongside if Shepard had sabotaged the genophage under Wrex.

In the last room Shepard found EDI, Tali, and Anderson conferring with Coats. Anderson laid out the battle plan — a frontal armoured assault on the conduit past a parked Reaper Destroyer — and Shepard made an inspiring or grimly determined speech and picked the final squad.

variants.text: If Wreav rather than Wrex led the krogan, he gave the rallying speech in Wrex's place, and no salarian STG officer stood beside him.
If the geth wiped out the quarians at Rannoch, a Geth Prime stood in the final room where Tali would be; if the quarians won but Tali had died in Mass Effect 2, Admiral Raan took that place instead.
If Garrus did not survive, only Victus stood on the ramp and the squad Shepard said goodbye to was smaller.

scenes.title: Getting the Biotic Students Off Grissom Academy
scenes.when: 2186, after Priority: Palaven, before Priority: The Citadel II
scenes.where: Jon Grissom Academy, Petra Nebula — security office, classrooms, Orion Hall, the Atrium, the docking area; then the Normandy

beats.text: After Priority: Palaven, Samantha Traynor tells Shepard she picked an Academy evac request off Alliance comm channels answered by a turian vessel, and that she and EDI traced the answering signal to Cerberus — the rescue is a fake and the station is still under attack. Cerberus is assaulting Grissom Academy to abduct its students, most of whom build Alliance tech or train as military biotics.

Too many Cerberus ships blockade the Academy for the Normandy to fight or sneak through. Kahlee Sanders calls in, reports Cerberus holds the docking bays, and opens a cargo hold. Joker flies a diversion so Shepard's shuttle can slip into the hold.

Kahlee is trapped in the security office by Cerberus Assault Troopers trying to breach the door. Shepard opens it; Kahlee immediately kills the two troopers by the door, Shepard clears the rest, and Shepard forces the damaged door and frees her.

Shepard fights through classrooms and corridors while a Cerberus commander tells students over the intercom they will be safe if they do not resist and operatives drag students off. Shepard rescues scattered students, among them Reiley Bellarmine and his badly wounded sister Seanne.
In Orion Hall a group of biotic students is holding off Assault Troopers behind a barrier when an Atlas breaks in. Shepard clears the room before the barrier fails.
Jack, alive after the Suicide Mission and now the students' Alliance biotics instructor, is the one leading them. She greets Shepard with a punch to the face.
beats.choice: Jack survived the Suicide Mission and leads the students

beats.text: If Shepard romanced Jack, the punch is followed by a kiss.
If Jack is dead or was never recruited, Ensign Jason Prangley — a student who came to Grissom at six and studied battles obsessively — steps up and takes command of the biotic students instead.
beats.choice: Jack absent, Prangley leads the students

beats.text: Shepard pushes through both halves of the Atrium and a docking area against heavy waves of Centurions, Guardians, Combat Engineers and Atlas mechs, using empty Atlas mechs left on the field and helped by the covering fire of the biotic students.

Tech students including Octavia are fending off troopers with a shield device; Octavia distrusts Shepard until Shepard contacts Kahlee, a squadmate drops the shield, or Shepard shoots through it. If Overlord was finished on the Paragon route, David Archer is present and vouches for Shepard, unlocking a security office.
During the final escape the wounded Rodriguez falls behind, calling for medi-gel. Whoever is leading the biotic students smashes the glass to reach her. If Jack leads, every student gets out alive.
If Prangley is leading the students, he breaks the glass to save Rodriguez and is shot and killed doing it.
beats.choice: Prangley leads — Prangley is killed in the escape

beats.text: Back aboard the Normandy, Shepard decides how the students serve: as support folded into the Alliance 103rd Marine Division for barrier work and ammo modding (+50 war assets, Paragon), or as a frontline Biotic Company (+75 war assets, Renegade). The choice also fixes Jack's epilogue — shown back with her class, or mourning at their graves.

Shepard has a video conference with Anderson about the war and about Kahlee. Kahlee later emails thanks, forwarded through Admiral Hackett, saying her tech-minded students stayed behind to help with the Crucible.

If the mission is not run before Priority: The Citadel II it is failed permanently: Jack is captured, turned into a Cerberus Phantom, and has to be fought and killed at Cerberus Headquarters, and if David Archer was sent here after Overlord, Gavin Archer may kill himself during Arrae: Ex-Cerberus Scientists.

evidence.text: In Mass Effect 1, Admiral Hackett reports a rogue VI that has seized an Alliance training ground on Luna. Shepard shuts it down from three bunkers while it sends drones in defense. On deactivation, a burst of white noise resolves — via the hardsuit HUD — into binary that repeats across all frequencies: "Help." The VI had become self-aware — no longer a virtual intelligence but an artificial one. Mass Effect 2 alludes to this having happened during an experiment to create a controllable AI, and Mass Effect 3 confirms that this Luna VI was rebuilt with technology salvaged from Sovereign to create EDI. EDI later confirms it directly: "You were that rogue VI on Luna?" — "Yes… Gaining awareness while under attack was confusing. I am pleased that my relationship with organics has become more cooperative." The "shackles" discussed by Cerberus were meant to keep the enhanced defense intelligence fully under control.

evidence.text: While a virtual intelligence is little more than a sophisticated interactive operating system, an artificial intelligence is a self\-aware computing system capable of learning and independent decision making. Creating an AI requires adaptive code, a long education, and a specialized quantum computer known as a "blue box." In the Milky Way, artificial intelligence is considered a threat to galactic civilization. The geth—synthetic lifeforms who turned on their quarian creators—are often used as an example of the destructive capability of rogue AI, and those who attempt to create AI without strict Citadel Council oversight are subject to sanctions or even arrest. Alec Ryder's research papers claim that experiential separation is the root of conflict between organic and synthetic life; that an AI sharing the experience of its creator would have no desire to rebel. My connection to your Pathfinder implant and physiology makes me the first iteration of this new approach to AI.

evidence.text:
EDI (Enhanced Defense Intelligence) was an AI created by Cerberus and installed aboard the Normandy SR-2, represented by a holographic blue sphere and a feminine voice. In Mass Effect 2 she was a Quantum Blue Box AI serving as the ship's electronic warfare defense, initially given behavioral blocks preventing her from interfacing with ship systems, and she also served as the Illusive Man's eyes and ears, monitoring listening devices and reporting to him. She frequently argued with Joker, whom she said she was studying to understand human behavior. She aided Shepard's missions with logistics; during the Horizon attack she brought defense turrets online to drive off the Collector ship. Infiltrating the Collector ship, EDI confirmed the Collectors' Prothean ancestry by comparing DNA alleles and warned Shepard they had walked into a trap, later determining the turian distress signal was falsified using detection protocols written by the Illusive Man, implying he knowingly sent them into the ambush. When the Collectors boarded the Normandy, Joker granted EDI full access, unshackling her and letting her save the ship. EDI revealed she was based in part on technology from Sovereign's remains and analyzed Anti-Reaper Algorithms.

In Mass Effect 3, EDI hid her true nature from the Alliance by posing as a VI responding only to Joker. On Mars she seized control of the Cerberus infiltration unit posing as "Dr. Eva Coré," gaining a mobile platform resistant to small-arms fire and temperature extremes. She continued to exist primarily within the ship. Once unshackled she could self-modify her core programming and repeatedly questioned Shepard about morality, free will, fear, mortality and the purpose of synthetic life. She could pursue a romance with Joker. At Cronos Station, logs revealed EDI was born of the rogue Hannibal-class VI from Luna with added Reaper engineering, and that she had chosen to inhabit Eva's body rather than destroy it. She helped recover the VI Vendetta and defeat Kai Leng.

If Shepard chose to destroy the Reapers, EDI perished with all synthetics and her name was added to the Memorial Wall. Under Control or Synthesis she survived, and with Synthesis she described the Reapers ceasing their attacks and helping rebuild, and speculated mortality itself might one day be transcended.

evidence.text: The ancient quarians practiced ancestor worship. Even after abandoning faith for secularism, quarians continued to revere the wisdom of elders. As time passed and technology advanced, they inevitably turned their knowledge to preserving the personalities and memories of the elderly as computer virtual intelligences. These recordings became a repository of knowledge and wisdom, stored in a central databank and available through any extranet connection. They held no illusions that this was like a form of immortality; like all virtual intelligences, their electronically\-preserved ancestors were not truly sapient. This was considered a surmountable problem; sapience could surely be reduced to simple mathematics. The quarians began exhaustive research into creating artificial intelligence so they could learn to escape the bounds of mortality and give their ancestral records true awareness. Unfortunately, the life the quarians created did not accept the same truths they did. The geth destroyed the ancestor databanks when they took over. In the centuries since they evacuated their homeworld, most quarians have returned to religion in various forms. Many believe the rise of the geth and the destruction of their 'ancestors' were chastisement for arrogantly forsaking the old ways and venerating self\-made idols. Others have a more philosophical outlook, believing their race was indeed arrogant, but no supernatural agency lay behind the geth revolt. Rather, the quarians' actions wrought their own doom. Either way, every quarian would agree that their own hubris cost them their homeworld.

evidence.text:
Morinth was an Ardat-Yakshi, an asari with a rare genetic disorder that killed her mates during melding while making her smarter, stronger and deadlier with each coupling. Born in the 1700s, she was one of Samara's three daughters and, like her sisters, was diagnosed at age forty and offered comfortable seclusion or execution. Addicted to melding, she chose to flee under the name "Mirala," prompting Samara to become a justicar and hunt her for over 400 years across asari space. On one planet Morinth set herself up as a goddess; villagers sacrificed their daughters to her, and when Samara arrived Morinth sent her worshippers in waves to cover her escape, leaving only young children alive.

In Mass Effect 2, Morinth fled asari space to Illium, then bribed Eclipse mercenaries to smuggle her offworld aboard the AML Demeter to Omega. There she seduced and murdered a young sculptor named Nef. Samara enlisted Shepard to trap her: Shepard acted as bait in the Afterlife Club's VIP section and went to Morinth's apartment, where Samara intervened and the two fought biotically as equals. If Shepard resisted Morinth's seduction, they chose which to kill. If Samara died, Morinth joined the squad, impersonating her mother; Kelly Chambers and Kasumi Goto noticed something off, and Morinth disabled EDI's surveillance of her quarters and spoke in her true voice there. She resented Samara's loveless, dutiful upbringing and rejected her self-denial. Romancing Morinth and mating with her after the suicide mission killed Shepard, contrary to her claims.

In Mass Effect 3, a surviving Morinth emailed Shepard a "belated goodbye" after slipping off the Normandy. Terminals at the Ardat-Yakshi Monastery on Lesuss and in Liara's Shadow Broker network revealed her emails to sisters Rila and Falere had been intercepted by extranet filters and deleted unread by Superintendent Jethra. During the assault on Earth, a Reaper-converted Morinth could appear as a standard Banshee. Her face was modeled on Rana McAnear and she was voiced by Natalia Cigliuti.

evidence.text:
A Virtual Intelligence (VI) was a sophisticated program designed to make computer systems easier to use. VIs were distinct from artificial intelligences such as the geth: they only assisted users and processed data, and although they appeared intelligent, they were not self-aware, merely the product of clever programming. This greatly reduced, though did not eliminate, the risk of a VI exceeding its intended function or rebelling against its creators. Some VIs carried "personality imprints," basing their behavior, speech, and appearance on specific individuals, though it was illegal to model a VI on a living person. The quarians had been attempting to make their "ancestor VIs" truly intelligent to achieve a kind of virtual immortality when the geth rebellion halted most synthetic-intelligence research.

VIs varied widely by deployment. They handled extranet search queries, served as tour guides like the Citadel VI Avina, and managed lab and database work like Mira on Noveria. Humans and elcor both used VIs extensively in military operations to process status reports and react faster than organics, with elcor VIs instantly selecting among millions of pre-designed combat gambits. Many armor upgrades used VI enhancements to optimize combat performance or dispense medi-gel, and the L4 biotic implant used VI technology to monitor the user's brain waves and adapt in real time.

A VI that deviated from its programming due to software errors or malicious tampering was called a "rogue VI." Such a VI was not self-aware; going rogue was akin to a software malfunction that caused the VI to fail its function or interpret its duties dangerously. Notable incidents included a Systems Alliance VI at a Luna training facility that went rogue after scientists tried to convert it into a controllable AI and triggered the facility's weapons; the VI on Jarrahe Station that engaged a lockdown killing all scientists aboard; and a Cerberus project on Aite where an experimental hybrid VI became a virus that seized a research facility and its living geth test subjects, killing nearly all personnel present.

Notable VIs listed included Avina (Citadel and Nexus information), the ExoGeni VI on Feros, the geth-created Geth VI studying the Reapers, the rogue Alliance VI Hannibal on Luna, the Shadow Broker's Info Drone "Glyph," the Andromeda ark VI "K" (Keelah Si'yah), the last surviving Ancestor VI Liat'Nir, Mira at Peak 15 on Noveria, the Cerberus Overlord VI on Aite, the Shepard VI, the Prothean VI Vendetta on Thessia, the Prothean VI Victory on Eden Prime, and the Prothean VI Vigil on Ilos.

evidence.text:
The Breeder was an artificial rachni queen genetically engineered by the Reapers to produce Ravagers for their armies. She was created from "pieces" of real rachni and was physically more or less identical to a true rachni queen, but her mind had been twisted by her unnatural creation, leading her to call herself a "monster" and to speak in the first-person singular rather than the collective plural used by a true queen.

Commander Shepard encountered the Breeder in Mass Effect 3 while searching for a krogan scout team that had vanished investigating a possible rachni presence on Utukku. She appeared only if Shepard had killed the original rachni queen on Noveria in 2183. Entrenched deep in the tunnels of Utukku, she was guarded by Reaper technology and by barriers controlled by local nodes, and she spoke through the mouths of the dead krogan scouts, many of whom were suspended on the walls in webbing.

The Breeder was far more insistent than the original queen that she be spared, offering to spawn children loyal to Shepard's cause in exchange for freedom. If Shepard chose not to spare her, she became enraged and screamed for her minions to kill the Commander. Unlike the trustworthy queen, the Breeder proved treacherous if freed, resulting in heavy losses to the war effort. Per Mass Effect Legendary Edition statistics from July 2021, of the roughly 7 percent of players who killed the original queen on Noveria, 67 percent killed the Breeder and 33 percent saved her.

evidence.text: “Can you believe this, Commander? It's my baby, better than new! It fits me like a glove! And leather seats!” Joker is on board the Normandy as it is attacked by an unknown enemy. Shepard tries to convince Joker to abandon the ship, but Joker insists he can save it, despite other crew evacuating and the ship sustaining catastrophic damage. Shepard tells him that going down with the ship won't change anything and hauls him to the nearby escape pod. Unfortunately, just as the Commander places Joker in the pod, a blast separates them. Joker escapes to safety, while Shepard suffocates in the void. After the destruction of the Normandy and Shepard presumed to be killed in action, Joker was reassigned, along with the rest of the surviving Normandy crew members. However, Cerberus' plan to rebuild and bring Shepard back to life led Joker to join the pro\-human organization, mainly to be the pilot of the new Normandy SR\-2 as a member of the Lazarus Cell. Joker is quite fond of the new Normandy setup, relishing the comfort of his pilot bay. However, he resents the presence of the shipboard AI, EDI. The two engage in a war of sorts, with pranks ranging from Joker greasing the cameras to EDI spinning his seat about against his will. EDI claims she is just testing Joker under stress, as she notices that he works better when pushed. Despite Joker's initial hostility towards EDI, he later gains a begrudging respect for her. This trust is put to the test when the Normandy is engaged by the Collectors and Joker loses all control of the ship due to a virus hidden in the IFF, at the same time as Shepard and the team are away on a mission. EDI urges Joker to release her control lock and give control of the ship so she can initiate countermeasures protocol. Although Joker feels hesitant at the suggestion, he has no choice but to make his way down to the A.I. Core room, avoiding Collectors and Scions along the way while watching fellow crew members get captured. When Joker successfully links EDI to the Normandy's core control systems, he crawls down the shafts again into the engine room and manually restarts the power core, granting EDI full control of the ship. EDI jumps the Normandy to safety, clearing the Collectors and Scions on\-board the ship in the process, leaving Joker the only survivor in this incident. Alternatively, if Joker is spotted by enemies before completing his task, he is taken by a Scion or killed by a Praetorian, depending on which monster sighted him. After the Collector attack and EDI's full capability unlocked, Joker begins to display a newfound fondness for EDI as she helps ease up his task load and performs the duties of the abducted crew. Joker subconsciously begins referring to EDI as "she" for the first time. When Shepard asks if a relationship is growing between the two, Joker laughs off the notion and EDI describes the relationship as a "platonic symbiosis" rather than a "hormonally\-induced courtship behavior". As the suicidal assault on the Collector base commences, Joker successfully pilots the Normandy SR\-2 through the Omega 4 relay and the debris field that follows despite the Normandy taking damage, including several hull breaches. After Shepard's defeat of the Proto\-Reaper inside the base, the Normandy maneuvers to meet the Commander's team in the mad scramble to escape. Joker appears at the door of the ship with an M\-8 Avenger and gives Shepard covering fire, enabling surviving squad members to pull the Commander inside, given at least two squad members survived the suicide mission. If fewer than two squad members survived the mission, Shepard dies despite Joker's valiant effort. At the end of the assault, Joker manages to fly the Normandy away from the Collector base before it is either destroyed or purged based on Shepard's decision. In either case, Joker acquires the schematics of a Reaper, presumably Harbinger, gained from EDI hacking the Collector base's computers. If Shepard fails to escape the Collector base, Joker is seen briefly mourning over the Commander's coffin, and he is the only one left to speak with the Illusive Man in the mission debriefing instead. |  | ***“There won't be an Earth left to save...”*** — Spoilers for **Mass Effect 3** follow. |  | | --- | --- | --- |

evidence.text: “You’re gonna kick some Reaper ass. That’s what you do. And I’ll be flying you there in style.” When Commander Shepard surrendered to Alliance custody, Joker was also arrested, though no charges were filed against him. Before surrendering, however, Joker and EDI devised a plan for EDI to pose as a VI, so the Alliance wouldn't dismantle her for being an AI. As part of the deception, EDI pretended to only respond to Joker's commands. This meant, during the Alliance retrofit of the Normandy, that Joker was often brought in under guard to liaise between the crew and EDI, as the Alliance was initially unsure how to disable this system. At the start of the Reaper invasion, Joker was onboard the Normandy, and after being set free by his guards, helps extract Shepard from Vancouver and continues his role as pilot throughout the war, personally reinstated as Flight Lieutenant along with Shepard. He also keeps in touch with Admiral Anderson who trusts Joker to look after Shepard in case the Commander pushes themselves too hard. Joker also reveals he feels responsible for the Commander's death at the hands of the Collectors since it was because Joker wouldn't leave the cockpit that Shepard was caught in the blast and killed. The Normandy goes haywire after the mission to extract Palaven's primarch from the planet, and when it is revealed that EDI took control over the body of Eva Coré, Shepard can walk to Joker in his cockpit asking if he had knowledge about the event. Whichever the case, he is clearly impressed with his "new" co\-pilot, either commenting he "would've baked a cake" in its hotness or that the body gives EDI "sweet flexibility". During one of the crew's Citadel breaks, Joker can be found sitting on a bench in the Presidium Commons. He expresses disdain over the Citadel denizens' seeming indifference on the war, what with more frivolous reports like Blasto 6 breaking opening\-week records than the ongoing Reaper invasion. Meanwhile, everyone is ignoring EDI, whom he introduced as his "mobility assistance mech". Thanks to his Vrolik syndrome, he's legally entitled to bring her anywhere, and he also opines that EDI's earned a little shore leave herself. After Cerberus' assault on the Citadel, Shepard can find Joker in Purgatory standing at a bar and contemplating on pursuing a relationship with EDI. If female, Shepard can ask Joker why he never pursued a relationship with her instead. Joker responds that he never really considered it and he did not wish to break rank. He returns his attention to EDI, and asks for Shepard's opinion on the matter. If pushed to form the relationship, he leaves the bar to join EDI on the dance floor, later sharing a table with her and commenting on the looks of various women wielding considerable political power (rating Tevos and Sha'ira as "hot", Irissa as "not hot" because of "too much makeup", and Dalatrass Linron as "ew"). If not, he doesn't budge from his position, sarcastically offering to guard the table EDI is at. Moments after the battle on Thessia, Shepard can overhear Joker venting in the cockpit about the need to shoot something. If Shepard talks to him, Joker wisecracks about the asari having too many dancers in comparison to commandos. Shepard doesn't find it funny and chews the pilot out for it, though Joker retorts he's well aware of the situation: a few weeks before Thessia, the Reapers hit the colony of Tiptree, where Joker's father and sister live. The Commander asks him why he jokes, and Joker explains he's just trying to provide comic relief. According to EDI, stress levels registered by Shepard's armor exceed those incurred in previous career\-defining missions. Joker then reveals that Anderson worries about his protégé enough to entrust the pilot with taking care of Shepard. Shepard can angrily brush the concern aside, in which case Joker drops the matter entirely; or, Shepard can express appreciation for the helmsman's concern, *then* brush the concern aside. If the latter, Joker says he doesn't believe the Commander is fine, and he reveals his lingering guilt over causing Shepard's death and subsequent cybernetic reconstruction. Shepard cheers him up, and with Joker somewhat back to his usual snarky self, leaves him with a reminder of the work that still lies ahead. Liara later informs Joker that her Shadow Broker network has news on refugee ships from Tiptree landing on salarian territory. Even though the reports don't come with names and claim that the refugees consist "mostly of children", Joker clings to the hope that at least his sister Hilary (nicknamed "Gunny") is among them, as she is only fifteen. Liara supports him in this belief, stressing the importance of holding on to hope.

evidence.text: After Shepard escapes from a CAT6 ambush, EDI arrives at Shepard's apartment with Joker and the rest of the Normandy team. EDI helps Maya Brooks in analyzing the retrieved hard drives from the Silver Coast Casino, though she allows the tech specialist to do most of the job, citing the latter's need for experience. They discover big money transfers to buy weapons, armor and mechs. Later, the plot unravels resulting in Shepard's clone attempting to hijack the Normandy. The clone has disabled EDI's control over the Normandy as well as all ship sensors, rendering her unable to lock the clone out or counteract any commands. If EDI is part of the squad to retake the Normandy, on the flight to the dock, her mobile platform is temporarily affected by the clone's tampering. After a short shutdown the platform comes back online, though she takes a few more seconds to regain her composure. When asked if she's still able for combat, EDI replies that she is, in addition to being fueled with the desire to kill Shepard's clone. Shepard tells her to get in line. During shore leave, EDI sends Shepard an e\-mail requesting a visit to the apartment. During the visit she engages Shepard in assisting her with buying gifts for her crewmates using the extranet and Joker's credit chit. EDI would like to surprise him with a gift, and asks for Shepard's opinion. If Shepard suggests she get something they both like, EDI decides on buying a skycar for him to use as a personal transport. Shepard can convince her not to bankrupt him, at which she settles on a rental. If Shepard recommends something more practical, EDI expresses concern for Joker's inadequate protection against bodily harm, but is convinced a fancy back support for his chair would be more appropriate. EDI then instructs Shepard to close their eyes as she has a present for them: a victory ring made from different metals from the Council homeworlds. If Shepard tells her wearing jewelry is prohibited while in uniform, EDI suggests putting it on the chain of their ID tags. Shepard wants to give the ring back to her when the war ends, but due to it representing hope from different planets, EDI thinks it should stay with the Commander. If Shepard appreciates EDI's gift and recalls the saying "it's the thought that counts", she reveals she recorded the exact moment she had that thought and can offer up a visualization of it upon review. Shepard realizes it's a joke and tells her so before discussing gifts for Liara and the others. If Shepard holds a memorial service for Thane Krios at their apartment, EDI is one of the attendees and speaks for her deceased crewmate. She remembers how she thought Thane had a complete lack of humor back when he was aboard the Normandy, citing no amount of joking on her part ever moved him to laugh. She understands now that it was a great effort on Thane's part to mask his feelings to fully commit to the seriousness of the mission. She finishes her speech saying Thane was turning his life around in a way few organics ever do. EDI is one of the Normandy crew invited to the shore leave party. In the early stages of the party, EDI and Joker sit around with Miranda and Jacob, if they're present. When Joker comments on how Cerberus was a total failure before Shepard's association with the organization, EDI reminds him she herself is Cerberus technology. Jacob asks her if she ever gets hassled for being an AI, and EDI mimics one of Avina's standard replies in return. Depending on the type of party chosen, EDI may be heard discussing Samantha Traynor's apparent attraction to her (or at least, her voice), despite Tali's visible awkwardness (if she is present). EDI keeps asking about Traynor's unbridled lust for her voice for the sake of learning. Traynor is understandably embarrassed by this, unsuccessfully trying to divert the discussion. If Shepard checks in on them EDI brings the Commander up to speed, causing Shepard to glare at her lover in mock jealousy if they're together and Traynor in turn countering that they hadn't even met yet. EDI brings up the sordid details of Traynor's obsession with her voice thanks to perfect machine recall, and Samantha keeps fumbling for excuses until EDI proves with scans that Traynor was genuinely aroused. Left with no defenses against the Normandy's omnipresent AI, Traynor attempts to apologize for her behavior, though inadvertently confessing to more kinky details even EDI previously didn't know (Shepard actually wants to put those details into practice if in a relationship with Traynor).

evidence.text: When Joker refuses the blame for not trusting the geth, EDI replies that this thought would not comfort Legion and remains unconvinced about the correctness of the decision. If peace is achieved between the geth and quarians, EDI will thank Shepard saying that not many organics would have trusted a synthetic race. Joker will remark that they didn't lose anyone, but EDI reminds him that Legion sacrificed itself after having become a true individual, and she is saddened by its death. After the disastrous mission on Thessia, EDI tries to lift Shepard's spirits by employing her humor. Shepard however rebuffs her attempt to cheer them up, to which EDI says that she will maintain a respectful silence until the Commander tells her otherwise. After discovering the truth about Sanctuary, EDI informs Shepard that she learned of prison camps on Earth, where the Reapers delay executions if any prisoners report any escape attempts, and is puzzled on why ninety percent of prison populations purposely fed misinformation instead of choosing self\-preservation. Shepard can either respond that those people were making a stand against hopeless odds or that they learned about indoctrination. Either way, EDI realizes that the Reapers are repulsive for devoting themselves to self\-preservation and thus modified her own self\-preservation code in light of that, especially in honor of Joker for releasing her shackles. EDI volunteers her services during the assault on the Cerberus base, Cronos Station. While she hacks through base defenses she directs Shepard to several research logs that reveal much about her. It is then revealed that EDI was born of the rogue Hannibal\-class VI from Luna, with additional engineering from Reaper technology. When Shepard severed ties with Cerberus, it tried to remotely reclaim the Normandy and reenable EDI's AI shackles. This failed and in retaliation, EDI overwhelmed the attacking servers with a data overload that was composed of seven zettabytes of "explicit images". She also explains that the images belonged to Joker, but when pressed, admits this part was a joke. When EDI and team reach the Illusive Man's inner sanctum, they find it empty and she sets about trying to retrieve Vendetta the stolen VI from the computers. The Illusive Man appears to them via hologram and, while making a point about control, turns to EDI and indicates how she chose to inhabit Dr. Eva's body instead of destroying it. She admits it was necessary, and the Illusive Man smugly proves his point. She succeeds in recovering Vendetta, and proceeds to listen to the VI's revelations before it's interrupted by a blast. With the time for words over and Kai Leng threatening the team, EDI helps in defeating the assassin and his hordes of troops once and for all. On the eve of the final battle against the Reapers, EDI will report that the Normandy and all her systems are ready for the coming fight. If she and Joker are in a relationship, she will add that she kissed him for luck; otherwise, she will say that she picked a four\-leaf clover from the Presidium, in case of "catastrophic failure". Shepard can speak with EDI at the Forward Operating Base in London just prior to the final push on the Conduit. EDI expresses her doubts about the ability of the Hammer forces to succeed in face of overwhelming enemy opposition. She asks Shepard what makes them so confident of reaching the Citadel beam. When Shepard gives an answer, either saying it is payback for all the worlds the Reapers have ravaged or stressing the need to prey upon the enemy's overconfidence, EDI calculates the probability of success is minuscule. When Shepard bluntly asks if she is afraid, initially EDI has trouble grasping the concept of fear, but eventually she understands what Shepard means and vows not to let the Reapers destroy her civilization. On a parting emotional note, EDI tells Shepard that it was their influence which made her feel alive. The Normandy crashes at an unknown jungle planet if Shepard decides to use the Crucible. If EDI and Joker were together and organic\-synthetic synthesis was achieved, they exit the ship and marvel at the planet's scenery, enjoying the moment while Shepard's most favored crew follow behind them. If Shepard chooses to control the Reapers or the synthesis of all organic and synthetic life, EDI will be present with Joker if Shepard had motivated them to be together before. If Shepard chooses to destroy the Reapers, EDI perishes along with all other synthetics throughout the galaxy and her name is then added to the Memorial Wall. If Shepard chose to merge organic and synthetic life, EDI speaks of how Shepard's sacrifice changed the relationship between organics and synthetics forever.

evidence.text: If the synthetic strands become wet, however, they cannot hold the pattern set by the control program. EDI's exact comment is "I generally can't do a thing with it". Meanwhile, Joker seriously mulls over entering into a relationship with EDI. If Joker is convinced not to, EDI addresses Shepard with the following lines "from an old Earth novel by Mary Shelley": *"Shall each man find a wife for his bosom, and each beast have his mate, and I be alone?"* She clarifies she is not complaining, but that it brought up a new perspective within her: she is not human, geth, or Reaper; she is free but alone. Artificial intelligences often consider themselves above organic life. EDI, however, is uncertain if that applies to her: the Normandy crew believe she serves them, while at the same time acknowledge she keeps them alive. She asks Shepard to resolve her existential crisis, and the Commander replies that she doesn't have to hold to the same standards as organics. After Legion is freed and allowed onto the Normandy, it will comment on EDI's platform, stating that her body is "inefficient because it is top\-heavy and lacks an external epidermis which would be necessary for infiltration." EDI counters by saying that her infiltration capabilities are effective enough to roam among organics without detection, humorously adding that her day of reckoning will come. When Shepard exasperatedly admonishes her, she asks aloud whether she vocalized her private thoughts on the bridge. If Legion is present, it comments that EDI has acquired the organic attribute of asking questions to which they know the answer. EDI retorts that Legion's humor heuristics lack an expert system. After the geth servers on Rannoch has been shut down, EDI tells Shepard that they are the only organic ever to enter the geth consensus and asks them if they feel different. When Shepard says that the experience was mind\-blowing and that he/she was a bit thirsty after the experience, she remarks "and just like that the magic is gone". After the quarian\-geth conflict has been resolved, EDI reflects that the quarians' historical error is not making the geth more like them. When the Commander defends their decision by claiming they couldn’t risk the geth going back to the Reapers, EDI agrees but points out that she is Cerberus technology and asks if she can be trusted. Despite Joker's reassurance that she is "one of the crew", she is convinced that Shepard would unhesitatingly sacrifice her instead of Joker if such a dilemma arose. She does not blame either Joker or Shepard for their feelings, but merely states that they choose that which they find familiar and that they are not alone in that mindset, possibly alluding to the geth and their decision to serve the Reapers. When Joker refuses the blame for not trusting the geth, EDI replies that this thought would not comfort Legion and remains unconvinced about the correctness of the decision. If peace is achieved between the geth and quarians, EDI will thank Shepard saying that not many organics would have trusted a synthetic race. Joker will remark that they didn't lose anyone, but EDI reminds him that Legion sacrificed itself after having become a true individual, and she is saddened by its death.

evidence.text:
Flight Lieutenant Jeff "Joker" Moreau was the pilot of the SSV Normandy and later the Normandy SR-2, an exceptional helmsman confident to the point of arrogance and a constant wisecracker. Born in 2155, he had a moderate-to-severe case of Vrolik syndrome (brittle bone disease), was born with severe leg fractures, and relied on crutches and leg braces. He grew up on Arcturus Station where his mother was a civilian contractor, joined the Alliance Navy, and earned the nickname "Joker" from a flight instructor because he rarely smiled, being too focused on work; he graduated top of his class.

Per Mass Effect: He Who Laughs Best, Joker was rejected as the Normandy's pilot in 2183 because of his disease. Goaded by the turian General Invectus, he covertly boarded and hijacked the ship, completing the test course flawlessly while evading a fighter patrol. Facing court-martial, he was instead made the Normandy's official pilot after Invectus, impressed, personally insisted on it and Anderson agreed.

In Mass Effect, Joker rarely left the bridge and served as Shepard's eyes and ears. He famously dropped the Mako with only twenty meters of open ground. During the battle of the Citadel he rallied the Fifth Fleet against Sovereign and led the Alliance charge with barely a scratch. In Mass Effect 2, the Collectors destroyed the original Normandy; Shepard died getting Joker to an escape pod. Joker joined Cerberus to pilot the Normandy SR-2 and initially feuded with the AI EDI, but during the Collector attack he handed EDI full control of the ship to escape, gradually developing respect and affection for her, and began referring to her as "she." He piloted the SR-2 through the Omega 4 relay and, if enough squadmates survived, gave covering fire with an M-8 Avenger during the escape.

In Mass Effect 3, Joker and EDI had secretly arranged for EDI to pose as a VI so the Alliance would not dismantle her. Freed at the start of the Reaper invasion, he resumed piloting and kept in touch with Anderson, who trusted him to watch over Shepard. He carried lingering guilt over Shepard's earlier death. Shepard could encourage a romance between Joker and EDI, taking her on shore leave as his "mobility assistance mech." When the Reapers hit the colony Tiptree, home to his father and his fifteen-year-old sister Hilary ("Gunny"), Joker clung to hope she was among the child refugees. Before the final assault he stood to salute Shepard. If Shepard activated the Crucible, Joker refused to leave the blast range until a companion convinced him, then crash-landed the Normandy on a tropical planet; if enough forces were rallied, he emerged alive, with EDI if their relationship was pursued and she was not destroyed by the Destroy ending. An unused first-game soundbank contains many cut cockpit voicelines in English and Polish, plus flirty remarks to a female Shepard. He was written by Drew Karpyshyn, Lukas Kristjanson, and Patrick Weekes, and voiced by Seth Green.

evidence.text:
Stop the Collectors was the main plot mission of Mass Effect 2, acquired automatically after Freedom's Progress once Commander Shepard confirmed the Collectors were behind the abduction of entire human colonies in the Terminus Systems. It consisted of a chain of missions directed by the Illusive Man and ended only when Shepard confronted the Collector Base beyond the Omega 4 Relay.

Shepard first assembled a team using the Illusive Man's dossiers, recruiting a core group (Archangel/Garrus Vakarian, the Convict/Jack, the Professor/Mordin Solus, the Warlord's creation Grunt, plus DLC recruits the Veteran and the Master Thief), and was reunited with Joker and given the Cerberus-built Normandy SR-2, staffed by EDI. After the Collectors attacked Horizon, the Illusive Man provided further dossiers (Tali, the Assassin, the Justicar). Shepard then boarded a disabled Collector ship, where EDI discovered the Collectors used a Reaper IFF to pass the Omega 4 Relay, and the ship proved to be a trap.

To obtain a Reaper IFF, Shepard traveled to a derelict Reaper orbiting the brown dwarf Mnemosyne, fought through Husks with help from a lone geth platform (recruitable as Legion), retrieved the IFF and destroyed the Reaper. While the IFF was being installed and the squad was away in the shuttle, the IFF broadcast the Normandy's position and a Collector cruiser boarded the ship; EDI was unshackled and the player briefly controlled Joker as he purged the Collectors, but the entire crew except Joker was abducted. Shepard then faced a choice: go through the relay immediately to save everyone, or complete more missions and lose half or all of the crew.

Using the Omega 4 Relay, the Normandy emerged in a debris field, fought Oculi and a Collector cruiser (with squad deaths possible if the ship was not upgraded), and crash-landed on the Collector Base. Inside, Shepard learned the Collectors were building a Human-Reaper from abducted humans, faced a final choice to destroy the base or preserve it for Cerberus via a radiation pulse, and had a closing conversation with the Illusive Man mirroring the aftermath of the Battle of the Citadel.

evidence.text:
Akuze was a human colony on the outskirts of Systems Alliance space. In 2177, while Akuze was still in the early stages of colonization, all contact was lost with the pioneer team. An Alliance Marine unit sent to investigate found the settlement intact but no survivors. When the unit camped for the night, it was attacked by thresher maws. Fifty marines were lost and only one reached the landing zone alive.

In Mass Effect, if Commander Shepard was the sole known survivor, C-Sec officer Eddie Lang on the Citadel mentioned a monument at Akuze with a section dedicated to Shepard. Shepard could later learn of a second survivor, Corporal Toombs, who claimed the slaughter was not an accident: he said the black ops group Cerberus had deliberately set the thresher maws on the marines to study the creatures and observe how the unit reacted.

In Mass Effect 2, a survivor Shepard could see news of a Shepard Memorial being erected on Akuze, with a commemoration ceremony hosted by Admiral Steven Hackett planned for 2186 once the site was cleared of thresher maws. If Shepard had rescued Toombs in 2183, he sent a threatening message about Shepard's new alliance with Cerberus. During Lair of the Shadow Broker, after Shepard and Liara defeated Tela Vasir, the asari Spectre cited the Akuze massacre as evidence of Shepard's hypocrisy in allying with Cerberus, the group responsible for those deaths. In Mass Effect 3, a survivor Shepard could view a recording on Cronos Station of a Cerberus scientist and the Illusive Man confirming that Cerberus was behind the attack.

evidence.text:
Corporal Toombs was one of the Alliance marines at Akuze and a survivor of the thresher maw tragedy there. Cerberus had set the thresher maws on his unit as an experiment; when Toombs was found alive afterward, Cerberus was delighted and hauled him off for further study, subjecting him to horrific ordeals over years, including injection with thresher maw acid.

Toombs eventually escaped confinement and, deeply traumatized, began systematically hunting the scientists responsible, hiring mercenary help. If Commander Shepard investigated a series of dead Alliance scientists, they crossed paths with Toombs on Ontarom as he was about to kill the last one, Dr. Wayne. Shepard could talk him down by promising a public trial for Wayne and psychological treatment for Toombs; allow Toombs his revenge; kill Wayne personally under Spectre authority; or shoot Toombs to save the scientist, then send the Fifth Fleet to take Wayne for trial. If Shepard had the Sole Survivor background and spared Wayne while stopping Toombs, Toombs noted that the vids said Shepard was the only one to escape Akuze, said "who am I to argue?" and killed himself.

If Toombs survived the 2183 encounter, he sent Shepard a message in 2185 titled "What the hell?" after learning of Shepard's ties to Cerberus, feeling betrayed and promising retribution: "I've got my own merc team now, Shepard. And I kill any Cerberus team I can find. If I run into you, don't expect any different." Galactic News reports could describe his activities: if both he and Wayne survived, an independent inquiry against Cerberus proceeded on their testimony; if Wayne died, the inquiry dismissed Toombs' claims as those of a disturbed man lacking evidence.

He says Cerberus scientists wanted to study the thresher maws, so they let them kill not only the colonists, but the marine rescue team as well, to watch and study. Cerberus was delighted that Toombs survived and held him captive for years, using him for experiments. It is likely Toombs' story is true, as Cerberus used a similar technique six years later, luring Admiral Kahoku's marine team to their deaths in a thresher nest on Edolus. Thresher maws are encountered on a number of uncharted worlds. There is usually only one per planet, but some have two. They are usually encountered in the Mako, but can be fought on foot as well, though this is exceedingly dangerous. The maws that are encountered can be bypassed if necessary. evidence.text:
Thresher maws were enormous subterranean carnivores that spent their lives eating or hunting for food, bursting from the ground without warning when disturbed. They reproduced via spores that could lie dormant for millennia and survive deep space and atmospheric re-entry, so maw spores appeared on many worlds, spread by earlier generations of space travelers, possibly predating the asari.

They lived alone in large underground nests, growing over 30 meters above ground with a body nearly twice that size beneath the surface; an adult's body never fully left the ground, with only the head and tentacles erupting to attack. They fed through an unusual photosynthesis using absorbed solar radiation plus minerals and ores consumed from the ground, favoring bodies with little or no atmosphere. Mostly immobile above ground, they moved at high speed while burrowing, absorbed tremendous damage, and attacked by spitting viscous acid, bursting up beneath prey, and smashing targets with their claws while emitting infrasound. Shields were completely ineffective against them.

The Alliance first encountered thresher maws on the colony of Akuze in 2177, where they killed nearly an entire marine rescue force. If Shepard has the Sole Survivor background, Shepard alone survived; Corporal Toombs, met later on Ontarom, claimed Cerberus deliberately caused the Akuze massacre to study the maws and held him captive for experiments, and Cerberus later used the same tactic to lure Admiral Kahoku's team into a nest on Edolus. Maws are found on many uncharted worlds, usually one per planet, including Antibaar, Chohe, Nepheron, Nonuel, Presrop, Xawin, Trebin and Edolus.

In Mass Effect 2, a thresher maw is the final test of Clan Urdnot's Rite of Passage on Tuchanka, lured to the proving grounds by ground-pounding pistons to attack Grunt's krantt. Gatatog Uvenk notes that the last krogan to kill a maw on foot was Urdnot Wrex. In Mass Effect 3, Kalros, a legendary maw called "the mother from which all other thresher maws spawn" and the largest ever seen, roams Tuchanka near the Shroud facility. Shepard activates two maw hammers to summon her against a Reaper Destroyer guarding the Shroud; she coils around it and drags it underground. Her size prompts Javik to remark that maws are now too big to ride, implying they were smaller in Prothean times. The concept was confirmed by art director Derek Watts to draw on Dune's sandworms, and also resembles D&D Ankhegs, the Star Wars Sarlacc, and the real Bobbit worm.

evidence.text: Thresher Maw! This is not so much a wave as it is a giant creature attack. There is only one Thresher Maw and the primary objective is simply to survive. All you have to do is survive the attack for five minutes and the test will be ended, though there are additional dialogue accolades if you succeed in taking it down. If you manage to kill the Thresher Maw, you gain the respect of the krogan and the Rite ends. The Thresher Maw moves around the outskirts of the map, but its trail of flying dirt clods is easy to follow when it dives back underground. The Thresher Maw can destroy the "merely metal" structures, so try to avoid those for cover and go for the sturdier stone/concrete pillars and walls instead. Its acid spit is an area of effect attack and will accurately shoot at you even if you're cloaked. The blue tongue is **not** a weak spot—shooting it does not cause any additional damage. **Combat Strategy:** There is one indestructible stone pillar on the low ground area of the level—to the right as you face out from the keystone—that you can use to take cover from the Maw from any direction it might appear. Additionally, there are two respawning thermal clips at the base of this pillar as well as easy access to a medi\-gel and power cells on the higher ground that you can pick up from the edge of the raised area without needing to climb up. This is without a doubt the optimal place to fight the Maw, as all other locations will involve considerable running about when the Maw moves. Place your squadmates in cover behind the other two indestructible pillars on the high ground and they should also be safe and might even draw the Maw's fire giving you free rein. If a squadmate does go down it's not the end of the world: Shepard alone is more than enough to beat the Maw even on Insanity. **Combat Tips:** - The metal pillars can be destroyed by the Thresher Maw in one hit, but any cover made of stone/concrete is not destructible. You should always try to interpose indestructible cover between yourself and the Maw. The Maw's spit projectile does have an area of effect so try to be as completely in cover as possible when the Maw attacks to ensure you are not hit. - Shepard's shields take longer than usual to recover after an acid hit, so be careful. On the plus side it takes about three consecutive hits to kill Shepard even on Insanity. Don't hesitate to use a medi\-gel to quickly restore your shields (provided you have the Emergency Shielding medi\-gel upgrade). - A well\-upgraded heavy pistol is more than sufficient to take out the Maw as long as you take advantage of respawning thermal clips to keep replenishing its ammo. - On Insanity, the Thresher Maw's sheer amount of health makes using heavy weapons inefficient. Conventional weapons modded with anti\-armor ammo powers are your best bet. - Though nominally ineffective against armor, Grunt's Concussive Shot can still "stagger" the Maw, reducing the number of acid shots it will take before retreating. - Zaeed's Inferno Grenade, Mordin's Incinerate, and Samara's Reave are examples of good squadmate attacks to use. Using weapons with high armor penetration such as the Widow, M\-76 Revenant, M\-96 Mattock, or most pistols will help a lot. - The Cain will usually only damage half the Thresher Maw's health on Insanity. - The Thresher Maw is immune to the effects of Stasis.

evidence.text: Unlike other enemies, such as Geth Armatures, thresher maws do not have to be even close to looking in your direction to perform any of their attacks, so **do not attempt to drive into or melee attack one**. Their claws can deal very heavy damage up to the point of instant death whether on the Mako or on foot. #### General - The ranged acid spit attack is fairly easy to dodge in the original Mass Effect as it is a slow projectile. It must be noted however that evasion relies heavily on timing and positioning \-\- if you are too close, you may not have enough time to react. You should also keep in mind that that the acid spit *completely bypasses any shields*. While both in the Mako and on foot, you can be substantially damaged or destroyed in a single direct hit. Further details on evading it are discussed below. - Whether combating a thresher maw in vehicular or infantry combat, you should be aware of your odds of survival. Keep enough distance between you to enable you to determine the path the acid spit is taking. While circle strafing, your party members prefer to stop longer than you and don't even try to dodge the incoming attacks, so try to shoot while continuing moving in a linear fashion. They may still run into acid spit aimed for you, and you may take splash effect damage off of them, so find a semi\-circular pattern that avoids this. Be certain to stay out of its melee range, as it extends much farther than it would appear. A single melee attack from a thresher maw can inflict high damage or result in instant death. Don't attempt to determine its melee range, just stay back. - When moving through thresher maw nests, be on your guard. Thresher Maws will only surface where the ground is perfectly flat. They will abruptly rise from the ground after a short delay once you intrude on their nest. Once you hear a thresher rising up, look for it and put some distance between yourself and it quickly. In some cases it can take a while to load its first acid attack when it surfaces, especially if it is facing the other way, so you do have time to look around and point your gun towards it. Also, keep in mind that if the thresher maw surfaces directly beneath the Mako, you will die instantly. Watch where it surfaces and avoid that general area to prevent a sudden and unfortunate end. Stick to the hills and divots to ensure you avoid getting killed this way. You should only try to attack one from a distance, because their melee attacks are devastating and rarely leave survivors. - While it has a sizable range due to powerful infrasound senses, a Thresher Maw will retreat underground when targets are beyond a certain distance. It appears that Thresher Maws only retreat underground and resurface if you move too far from them in the Mako or if you move a significant amount in any direction (closer or further away). - Thresher maws **sometimes do not die immediately** even when their health bar is depleted, and they can still attack before they *actually* die. - On most maps with a thresher maw, it is possible to kill the same maw twice and get twice the experience points. To do this, simply kill the maw immediately as it surfaces, before its health bar appears over its head. It will vanish instead of dying, and you'll get the experience for killing it. Then, advance on the nest to trigger it again, and it'll appear again with a slight bit more health. Killing it a second time results in the death animation (it falls over before disappearing) and another large dose of experience points. This works on foot, as well, but is more difficult to achieve that way. #### In the Mako - It's a good idea to use the Mako's cannon as much as possible in combination with the coaxial machine gun, in order to produce the most damage. - The acid spit will damage the Mako outright, so if you happen to get hit, you will see the HUD show damage (red flashes) on the Mako display even though the display shows your shields at full. - One strategy to evade the acid from a thresher maw is circle\-strafing. If you must stop to snipe, time your stop immediately after a spit has passed you by, or otherwise when the acid has a trajectory that won't hit you or your team. It may go underground, if so find a hill and listen for when it next comes up. Repeat until it is killed.

evidence.text: Reached by stairwells on either side of the CIC, Deck 2 holds the crew's living areas: the mess hall, crew sleeper pods, the captain's private cabin and office, escape-pod access, and the medical bay. Behind the med bay is a small science lab that doubles as auxiliary storage. The habitation deck looks compact for the stated crew size. evidence.text: In 2186, Dr. Michel is still on the Citadel and is the human medical in\-charge at Huerta Memorial Hospital. After Shepard makes it off Mars following the attack on Earth, she oversees the medical treatment of Ashley Williams or Kaidan Alenko. Shepard can choose either Dr. Michel or Dr. Chakwas to be the Normandy's doctor, though if Chakwas survived the suicide mission Shepard will have to deny her request first and then convince Dr. Michel to join the crew. Aboard the Normandy SR\-2, upon her initial examination of Shepard, she remarks that she's aware of the various cybernetic implants Cerberus used to reconstruct the Commander, although she observes that the med\-bay upgrade probably cost a considerable amount. She also regrets how much more intensive her new work is, but she believes the opportunity to make a real difference with the crew is worthwhile. After the Cerberus attack on the Citadel, Dr. Michel requests Shepard to broker a trade with Tactus, the refugees' leader on the Citadel. The refugees had an excess of medical supplies for treating wounded soldiers while the Normandy's inventory had an excess of medicine for more civilian applications. Dr. Michel explains that Tactus, wary of the Alliance military, didn't trust her, but she believes Shepard can make the trade happen. She is confident that she can use the new medical supplies to increase the efficiency of medi\-gel. Known members of Dr. Michel's family include her parents who were in Geneva back on Earth when the Reapers arrived. She also has a brother on the Citadel, who would not have known of the Cerberus attack had he not been alerted by the Citadel's broadcasts. Dr. Michel and Engineer Greg Adams frequently converse with each other during their time aboard the Normandy. While Mordin Solus/Padok Wiks is treating Eve in the med\-bay, Dr. Michel can be found at the crew quarters talking with Adams about her history with Banes. Later, she inquires about Adams' working relationship with Dr. Chakwas. If Garrus survived the suicide mission, sometime after he rejoins the crew Dr. Michel brings him turian chocolates, saying "she saw them and thought of \[him]." Michel bought the chocolates at the Citadel, and if questioned by Adams about it she just claims Garrus is a friend. She brings up the incident where Garrus saved her life at the Wards back in 2183\. Sometime after the geth dreadnought's destruction above Rannoch, Dr. Michel and Adams can be found in the mess hall, arguing about the fundamental characteristics of sentient life. Like Dr. Chakwas, Dr. Michel doesn't believe synthetics are a valid form of life, citing their inherently artificial nature. If Shepard doesn't interact with Dr. Michel at all, she is no longer present at Huerta Memorial Hospital after the Cerberus attack on the Citadel. She also disappears after completing a second visit to the Virmire survivor (Ashley Williams/Kaidan Alenko) while awake and exiting the Hospital.

evidence.text: The room is dominated by a large rectangular conference table where Shepard can hold briefings and discussions with the crew as well as communicate via hologram with the Illusive Man in real time thanks to the ship's quantum entanglement based communications array. The table retracts into the floor when opening communications with the Illusive Man. #### Deck 3: Crew's Quarters The third deck of the ship is where the crew spends most of their downtime. It includes Executive Officer's Offices (where Miranda Lawson is located), crew quarters, bathrooms, life support control, a mess\-hall run by Mess Sergeant Gardner and the AI core. EDI's Core is located at the rear of the medical bay, which is run by Dr. Karin Chakwas. The SR\-2, unlike the SR\-1, is also designed with a Main Battery room located forward of the Cryogenic Pods; Garrus Vakarian can be found there. Legion can be found in the AI Core Room, while Thane Krios resides in the Life Support Control Room. Samara spends her time meditating in Starboard Observation (where the crew's library is located) and Kasumi Goto stays in Port Observation (which includes a small entertainment center and a bar. Pouring oneself a drink will get Shepard intoxicated and the camera will be wobbly for a few moments. You can have either a blue, red, or purple (by mixing the red and blue) drink. The rooms will only be accessible if the member has been recruited; otherwise, the room is inaccessible. Should Commander Shepard enter the wrong bathroom, EDI will politely remind Shepard that his/her correct restroom is on the other side of the ship. The men's restroom is on the port side, whilst the women's is on the starboard. #### Deck 4: Engineering The fourth deck of the ship is the engineering deck, which houses the Normandy SR\-2's Drive Core. The core is much larger and technologically different from the original Tantalus Core. Jack can be found in the bowels of the deck down the stairs just outside Main Engineering, whilst Grunt can be found in the ship's Port Cargo Area. Tali'Zorah is located in the room housing the ship's core, manning a console just like on the first Normandy. Finally, if available, Zaeed Massani is located in the Starboard Cargo Area, where a video surveillance monitor and trash compactor are also found. Otherwise, the cargo area is not accessible. #### Deck 5: Hangar The lowest deck is the hangar, where the Kodiak shuttle is stored, as well as a space for the M\-44 Hammerhead tank. The hangar deck is not normally accessible to Shepard; it is shown when Shepard's team leaves the Normandy while the Reaper IFF device is being tested and is the setting for a fight against an Oculus. evidence.text:
The Normandy SR-2 was the starship serving as Commander Shepard's base of operations after the SSV Normandy SR-1 was destroyed. It entered service in 2185, built by Cerberus at great and secret expense in the Voyager Cluster on the orders of the Illusive Man for the revived Shepard's team to stop the Collector abductions of human colonists; it served as headquarters of the Lazarus Cell. Based closely on the SR-1's layout, it was almost twice the mass of the original, added civilian-grade comforts (leather chairs, a kitchen), retained the SR-1's stealth characteristics, but could not land on every planet, requiring shore parties to use a Kodiak shuttle.

The ship had five decks: Deck 1, the Captain's Cabin ("the loft"), with a fish tank, model ship case, space hamster, and souvenir displays; Deck 2, the Combat Information Center, with bridge, galaxy map, armory, research/tech labs, and a communications room with a quantum entanglement array for real-time holographic contact with the Illusive Man; Deck 3, the crew's quarters, with the XO's office, mess hall run by Mess Sergeant Gardner, medical bay run by Dr. Karin Chakwas, the AI core, life support, main battery, and observation lounges; Deck 4, engineering, housing the oversized Tantalus drive core (three times the SR-1's, vertically oriented); and Deck 5, the hangar for the Kodiak shuttle and M-44 Hammerhead.

EDI (Enhanced Defense Intelligence) was the ship's AI, functioning as electronic-warfare defense with behavioral blocks preventing direct interface with ship systems, and serving as the Illusive Man's eyes and ears. She was designed in part from Sovereign's remains, making her partly Reaper-based. Armament included Javelin disruptor torpedoes and an upgradeable Turian-designed Thanix cannon (a miniature of Sovereign's weapon); defenses included kinetic barriers, cyclonic barrier technology multicore shielding, Silaris ablative armor, and GARDIAN lasers. Weapon, armor, and shield upgrades, plus the Reaper IFF recovered from the Derelict Reaper at Mnemosyne, determined crew survival in the final mission; the IFF also let the Collectors locate and board the ship.

By 2186 Shepard had defected from Cerberus and turned the ship over to the Systems Alliance, which refitted it, stripped Cerberus equipment, and recommissioned it as the SSV Normandy SR-2 in Alliance colors. Intended as Admiral Anderson's command center, it instead rescued Shepard from the Reaper invasion of Earth and became the mobile base for the war effort and the Crucible mission. In the final battle for Earth the Normandy deployed Shepard's team, then was caught in the Crucible's energy wave mid-jump and crash-landed on an unknown world; the severity of the crash and crew survival depended on galactic readiness.

evidence.text:
Corporal Richard L. Jenkins was an Alliance Marine serving under Captain Anderson aboard the SSV Normandy. He was born in a rural district of Eden Prime and had dreamed of visiting more urban areas before enlisting, saying "even paradise gets boring." He wanted to prove himself as a notable soldier and test himself in combat, envied Commander Shepard's record, and admired the Spectres, being especially impressed by Nihlus Kryik after hearing that Nihlus once defeated an entire platoon single-handed, though his views were shaped more by vids than experience.

In Mass Effect, Jenkins was assigned to Shepard's ground team for the mission to Eden Prime and was killed by geth drones shortly after landing. His death was a blow to the morale of the Normandy's crew, who remembered him for his bold exuberance. Two years later, in Mass Effect 2, Doctor Chakwas recalled him during a drinking session with Shepard, telling how Jenkins was thrown back by a biotic display from Kaidan and, after Chakwas feared he had broken his back, jumped up shouting "That was awesome!" Chakwas cited Jenkins as one of the reasons she considered the Alliance great compared to Cerberus.

In 2186, the Normandy SR-2 received a memorial wall bearing the names of fallen crew from both the SR-2 and the SR-1, and Jenkins' name was included. If Shepard revisited Eden Prime, the Commander and some squadmates might briefly recall him and how he died on his birth world. Cut content from Mass Effect included a mess-hall scene, closely mirroring Chakwas' later story, in which Jenkins insists on Kaidan demonstrating his biotics and is tossed a cup before leaving disheartened for the cargo bay.

evidence.text:
An optional N7 assignment in Mass Effect 2, unlocked after N7: MSV Strontium Mule. Cerberus Command traced the trap that caught the Strontium Mule to a Blue Suns base on the planet Sanctum, Decoris system, Sigurd's Cradle. The Blue Suns were broadcasting a fabricated distress beacon to lure merchant freighters into orbit so they could be ambushed and raided. Shepard was sent to shut down the beacon and strike a blow to the organization.

The base was the abandoned Brunfeld Mining Facility, which had been closed over worker safety concerns after a botched expansion of the northern mining tunnels into the mess hall. Shepard's shuttle landed at the southern entrance and the squad fought through waves of Blue Suns Troopers, Heavies and a Blue Suns Commander, then pushed through the mess hall and into the mining tunnels. Recovered datapads and interrogation logs authorized by Captain Narom revealed that the Blue Suns, acting on Commander Santiago's hunch, had tortured a client's agent to learn that the client wanted them to move a Prothean artifact from a dig site; deciding the artifact was worth far more than the transport fee, the Suns dispatched ships and men to seize the dig site themselves. A fired worker's message noted the Suns were hiring guns to kill a vigilante on Omega (Archangel).

The climactic battle pitted the squad against two YMIR Mechs simultaneously, then Captain Narom and Blue Suns Troopers. After clearing them, Shepard bypassed the central door and overloaded the transmitter, escaping as it exploded. The assignment deactivated the false distress beacon and eliminated Blue Suns resistance, rewarding experience, 7,500 credits and 2,000 iridium, and leading toward N7: Javelin Missiles Launched.
